title: add-benchmark-lab-performance-suites-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v124
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Expand benchmark-lab coverage to capture multi-tenant representative workload behavior, add new profiling baselines for kernel-selection experiments, and wire up a resilient reporting pipeline that publishes per-run metrics to S3 and our observability bucket. This PR bundles three coordinated changes required to stabilize perf regression detection across recent runtime kernel changes.

Summary of changes: added a new performance test suite (perf_suites/multi_tenant_latencies) with representative workload runners that simulate mixed chat/generation/embedding traffic patterns; introduced profiling baselines for kernel-selection and kv-cache hot paths (profiling/baselines/v124) produced by earlier profiling runs; implemented a reporting pipeline (reporting/pipeline_v124) that aggregates runner outputs, normalizes latency distributions, computes p50/p90/p99 token latencies, and uploads artifacts and a summary JSON to the observability bucket; updated CI workflows to run lightweight versions of the representative runners on perf-canary and to validate reporting artifacts during PRs; added Grafana dashboard JSON and query templates for the new metrics.

Compatibility & rollout: new runners are opt-in by default; perf-canary schedules a daily full run using Dedicated tier credentials. The reporting pipeline includes a fallback mode that emits partial summaries when some runners time out; this avoids noisy failures while still surfacing available signals. No API or runtime surface-level breaking changes are included.

Testing & validation: unit tests for runner configs and parsers were added; integration tests run end-to-end in the benchmark-lab GCP project using a small-scale cluster (CI). We ran three full baseline runs across x86 and A100 fleets to produce the profiling baselines checked in under profiling/baselines/v124. CI checks validate artifact schema and a checksum of summary.json before merge.

Checklist: - [x] Add multi-tenant representative runners and workload configs - [x] Add profiling baseline JSON artifacts and metadata - [x] Implement reporting pipeline with retry/backoff and partial-summary mode - [x] Add CI validation and lightweight perf-canary job - [x] Add dashboards and query templates - [x] Run and commit baseline runs

Impact: should improve sensitivity of the regression detector to kernel selection changes and batching policy regressions, and enable faster triage by producing normalized, comparable summaries per run.

Notes: baseline artifacts are large; we store canonical baselines in the observability bucket and provide small representative samples in-tree for quick local runs.

review_comments: Ben Thompson: Left a few nits on runner config parsing (prefer explicit timeouts instead of None); questioned the default concurrency in multi_tenant_runner.
Aisha Kapoor: Addressed by setting explicit default timeouts and adding a concurrency flag. Added documentation note about cost when running full-suite.
Lina Morales: CI check failed initially due to schema mismatch in baseline_summary.json (missing 'kernel_version' field). Requested adding a schema test.
Aisha Kapoor: Added schema test and updated baseline_summary.json to include kernel_version and fleet metadata. Re-ran baselines and updated checksums.
Kai Zhang: Approved after verifying reporting pipeline handles partial-run cases correctly and S3 permissions are scoped to the perf-lab role.
CI Bot: perf-canary job initially failed on test timeout; rerun passed. All checks green.
release_notes: Added benchmark-lab v124: multi-tenant performance suites, profiling baselines for kernel-selection experiments, and a resilient reporting pipeline that publishes normalized summaries to the observability bucket. No breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: When enabling full runs in production, ensure the perf-lab GCP service account has s3/gcs write permissions and that per-run costs are budgeted. Dashboard is available at dashboards/benchmark_lab_v124.json.
